documents.title: Board Meeting Intimation for Corporate Announcement U/R 29(1)(A) Of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 Read With SEBI (PIT) Regulations, 2015 Regarding Intimation Of Holding The 3/2026-27 Board Meeting Scheduled To Be Held On Friday, 13Th Day Of November, 2026
Compliances-Certificate under Reg. 74 (5) of SEBI (DP) Regulations, 2018
Shareholder Meeting / Postal Ballot-Outcome of AGM

analysis.summary: Syncom Formulations (India) Limited reported a consolidated total income of Rs. 133.36 crore and a 59% increase in Profit Before Tax to Rs. 32.25 crore in Q1 FY2026-27, alongside financial results for the full year ending March 31, 2026. Management highlighted robust performance drivers, expanded scale across domestic and international segments, and adherence to quality manufacturing standards. The company proposed a dividend of 10% (Rs.

demand_outlook.claim: The company stated that the global pharmaceutical industry continues on its long-term growth trajectory notwithstanding an uncertain macroeconomic backdrop.
demand_outlook.quote: The global pharmaceutical industry continues on its long-term growth trajectory notwithstanding this uncertain macroeconomic backdrop.

demand_outlook.claim: Management noted that volume growth in emerging and pharma-emerging markets continues to outpace mature markets.
demand_outlook.quote: Volume growth in emerging and "pharma-emerging" markets - including India, China, Latin America and Southeast Asia - continues to outpace mature markets such as North America, Western Europe and Japan, where per capita consumption is already high and incremental growth is comparatively moderate.

demand_outlook.claim: The company pointed out that large-volume therapies under the National List of Essential Medicines continue to face price caps and periodic downward revisions.
demand_outlook.quote: Growth, however, remains uneven - large-volume therapies under the National List of Essential Medicines (NLEM) continue to face price caps and periodic downward revisions, even as faster value growth is concentrated in chronic and specialty segments such as oncology, anti-diabetics and, increasingly, the GLP-1 category, which is expected to see patent expiries and an estimated CAGR of over 30% through 2030.

demand_outlook.claim: Management stated that India's increasing life expectancy and growing elderly population highlight the need for preventive healthcare.
demand_outlook.quote: Adult vaccination ecosystem: India's increasing life expectancy and growing elderly population highlight the need for preventive healthcare.

demand_outlook.claim: Management stated that global medicine spending remains on course to exceed US$ 2.3 Trillion by 2028, supported by a projected CAGR of 5-8%.
demand_outlook.quote: Total pharmaceutical spending remains on course to exceed US$ 2.3 Trillion by 2028, supported by a projected CAGR of 5–8%.

demand_outlook.claim: The company noted that volume growth is expected to grow at an average rate of 2.3% through 2028, driven by emerging markets.
demand_outlook.quote: While volume growth plateaued in 2023, it is expected to grow at an average rate of 2.3% through 2028, driven by emerging markets such as China, India, Southeast Asia and Latin America.

demand_outlook.claim: India's pharmaceutical market is projected to see strong growth with medicine spending expected to reach US$ 38-42 Billion by 2028.
demand_outlook.quote: India’s pharmaceutical market is projected to see strong growth, with medicine spending expected to reach US$ 38-42 Billion by 2028, with a CAGR of 7–10% from 2024 to 2028.

margins_costs.claim: Management noted that elevated global energy prices, geopolitical tensions, and India's dependence on China for APIs have kept supply chains under pressure and intensified input cost fluctuations.
margins_costs.quote: Supply chain vulnerabilities: Elevated global energy prices, continuing geopolitical tensions and India's continued 70-74% dependence on China for APIs and key raw materials have kept supply chains under pressure, intensifying input cost fluctuations and creating risks to procurement stability and manufacturing costs.

margins_costs.claim: Management flagged that input costs face all-round increases due to inflation.
margins_costs.quote: Other challenges include stringent regulatory issues, government-mandated price controls, all-round increases in input costs due to ination, and the need to address talent shortages, particularly in STEM and digital roles, and to enhance intellectual property protection.

capital_allocation.claim: The Board of Directors recommended a dividend of Rs. 0.10 per equity share for the financial year 2025-26.
capital_allocation.quote: Your Board of directors are pleased to recommend a dividend of Rs. 0.10 per equity share, (i.e., 10% on the face value of Rs. 1/- each), for the financial year 2025-26, subject to the approval of the Members at the ensuing Annual General Meeting.

capital_allocation.claim: The company stated that it has not accepted any public deposit falling within the ambit of section 73 of the Companies Act, 2013.
capital_allocation.quote: Your Company has not accepted any deposit from the public falling within the ambit of section 73 of the Companies Act, 2013 read with the Companies (Acceptance of Deposits) Rules, 2014 and there were no remaining unpaid or unclaimed deposits as on 31st March, 2026.

capital_allocation.claim: The company transferred unclaimed and unpaid dividends of Rs. 3,59,089.86 and corresponding 5,25,538 equity shares for FY 2016-17 to the IEPF Authority.
capital_allocation.quote: Accordingly, Syncom has transferred the unclaimed and unpaid dividends of Rs.3,59,089.86 and has also transferred corresponding resulting 5,25,538 equity shares of Re.1/- each for the F.Y. 2016-17 to the IEPF Authority as per the requirement of the IEPF rules.

risks_headwinds.claim: Management highlighted that the pharmaceutical industry faces challenges from pricing regulations on drugs brought under the National List of Essential Medicines.
risks_headwinds.quote: Regulatory Price Controls: Pharmaceutical industry continues to face challenges from pricing regulations on drugs brought under the National List of Essential Medicines (NLEM), which impacts revenue potential and profit margins.

risks_headwinds.claim: The company reported growing threats from the increased availability and affordability of generic drugs driven by patent expirations and biosimilars.
risks_headwinds.quote: Growing threats of generics: The industry faces growing threats from the increased availability and affordability of generic drugs, driven by patent expirations, the rise of biosimilars, and India's own strong position as a major exporter of generic drugs.

risks_headwinds.claim: Management noted that underfunded public healthcare infrastructure, currency volatility, and geo-political conflict remain areas of concern.
risks_headwinds.quote: Notwithstanding this growth outlook, several structural challenges persist. Underfunded public healthcare infrastructure, currency volatility and continuing geo-political conflict remain areas of concern.

risks_headwinds.claim: Management noted that heavy increases in tariffs and penalties announced by the US may have an adverse effect on export performance.
risks_headwinds.quote: The heavy increase in tariffs and penalty announced by the US in July/August, 2025 the resulting for export in US market may be highly disappointed and may have adverse effect on the export front of the Company.

risks_headwinds.claim: The industry's continued dependence on China for Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients poses a strategic vulnerability.
risks_headwinds.quote: Furthermore, the industry's continued 70-80% dependence on China for Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) poses a strategic vulnerability despite government efforts to promote domestic API manufacturing.

risks_headwinds.claim: Management highlighted that proposed US tariffs, including a 200% tariff on pharmaceutical imports, could squeeze profit margins and reduce competitiveness.
risks_headwinds.quote: Critically, the Indian pharmaceutical industry faces potential disruption from proposed tariffs, including a 200% tariff on pharmaceutical imports by the US, which is India's largest drug importer (accounting for nearly 33% of India's pharma exports in FY2024).

management_commitments.claim: The company aims to enhance manufacturing capacities with world-class facilities.
management_commitments.quote: Enhancing manufacturing capacities with world-class facilities.

management_commitments.claim: The management committed to expanding the nutraceutical and injectable portfolio to cater to evolving healthcare needs.
management_commitments.quote: Expanding the nutraceutical and injectable portfolio to cater to evolving healthcare needs.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
